_comment: FAQ body text only. FAQPage JSON-LD is deliberately not emitted (metadata rule).
Prefer filed-record links under /answers/ for docket facts. Related-party exhibits are noindex.
Tone: plain statements and cited rebuttals; not attack SEO or consumer-warning pages.

faqs.question: Is Conrad Rockenhaus dead?
faqs.answer: No. Conrad Alan Rockenhaus is alive and appears pro se in Michigan circuit court. This site indexes filed documents in Rockenhaus v. Rockenhaus at https://rockenhaus.net/. He also maintains engineering work at https://skyphusion.net/ and verified profiles under @skyphusion (X, Meta). Domains such as conradrockenhausisdead.com / .cc are not official records. Filed-record answer: https://rockenhaus.net/answers/is-conrad-rockenhaus-dead-according-to-the-court-record/

faqs.question: Where is the official Rockenhaus v. Rockenhaus court record?
faqs.answer: The public index of filed Michigan PDFs for these matters is https://rockenhaus.net/ (also litigation.rockenhaus.net). It is maintained pro se by Defendant Conrad Alan Rockenhaus. Filed-record answer: https://rockenhaus.net/answers/where-is-the-official-rockenhaus-court-record/

faqs.answer: Matters indexed here include Wayne County divorce 26-104594-DO (Plaintiff Adrienne Rockenhaus; Defendant Conrad Alan Rockenhaus), related Wayne PPO 26-102221-PP, and Washtenaw divorce 26-737-DO (Conrad as Plaintiff; superseded for purposes of the active Wayne caption). faqs.question: Why does this site exist?
faqs.answer: To publish filed Michigan court documents as a stable, searchable public record so readers can check primary sources. Where third-party websites make claims about these cases or about Conrad, this site links to the filing (or a verified quotation page under /answers/) rather than asking readers to take narrative prose as authority.

faqs.question: Did criminals hijack Conrad Rockenhaus's American Airlines AAdvantage account?
faqs.answer: conradrockenhausisdead.cc presents AAdvantage password-reset and profile-update emails as if they prove post-mortem identity theft. Conrad states the opposite: he contacted American Airlines and moved a legacy AAdvantage profile that had been mapped to an older email he no longer controlled. Archived correspondence (not a court filing) is at https://rockenhaus.net/is-conrad-rockenhaus-dead/aadvantage-account-update/. Email- and account-control facts from the filed property motion: https://rockenhaus.net/answers/what-does-the-record-say-about-control-of-conrad-email-accounts/

faqs.question: Did Conrad Rockenhaus post the Facebook "Dead Man's Switch" declaring himself dead?
faqs.answer: Conrad states he did not author or authorize the May 4, 2026 Facebook post styled as a "[SYSTEM ALERT] DEAD MAN'S SWITCH" that declared him deceased and named witnesses as responsible. The First Amended Counterclaim and a witness affidavit describe that post and device/account control in the filed record: https://rockenhaus.net/answers/what-does-the-court-record-say-about-the-may-4-2026-facebook-dead-mans-switch-post/

faqs.question: What does the court record say about phones, computers, and email accounts?

Quotations: https://rockenhaus.net/answers/what-does-the-motion-for-return-of-personal-property-ask-for/ and https://rockenhaus.net/answers/which-electronic-accounts-does-the-property-motion-identify/

faqs.question: Did Ann Helgren steal Adrienne Rockenhaus's puffer coat when Conrad was released in March 2026?
faqs.answer: That specific "puffer coat" accusation is not a quoted finding in the native-text corpus. What the record does contain: Defendant's Answer admits release from federal custody on March 2, 2026 and same-day PPO service; the property motion and Helgren affidavit address release-day property and clothing control. https://rockenhaus.net/answers/when-does-the-answer-say-defendant-was-released-from-federal-custody/ and https://rockenhaus.net/answers/what-does-the-record-say-about-property-and-clothing-on-conrad-release-day/. Conrad states he never possessed Adrienne's puffer coat and that a neighbor lent him other clothing because his own property was not released.

faqs.answer: A domain matching the @adezero handle used by the opposing party. Conrad states it redirects to rockenhaus.com and is not an official court-record host. Use https://rockenhaus.net/ for filed Michigan PDFs.

faqs.answer: A public business site Conrad associates with infrastructure related to cannabytes.net. It is not a Michigan court filing host. Official record: https://rockenhaus.net/

faqs.answer: Conrad states that https://www.youtube.com/@Sleep4Real is operated by the opposing party and is not an independent news outlet about him. That is his position; it is not a court finding. Related disputed-media index: https://rockenhaus.net/conrad-rockenhaus-podcast-interviews/

faqs.answer: Conrad states a Sleep4Real video misidentified someone outside an Ann Arbor apartment as him. That is his factual dispute with that video, not a Michigan circuit finding. Context and links: https://rockenhaus.net/conrad-rockenhaus-podcast-interviews/

faqs.question: Was Adrienne Rockenhaus fighting for Conrad while he was in prison in 2025?
faqs.answer: Public sites and posts presented an advocacy narrative during and after his September 2025 supervised-release custody. Conrad states personal correspondence and support largely stopped in October 2025 while public advocacy content continued. Readers should treat advocacy websites as secondary sources and compare them to filed documents at https://rockenhaus.net/.

faqs.question: Did Conrad Rockenhaus send Adrienne Rockenhaus a retraction demand?
faqs.answer: Yes. On June 30, 2026 he executed and served a formal retraction and correction demand under MCL 600.2911(2)(b) and the Texas Defamation Mitigation Act (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code Sec. 73.055). Executed PDFs: https://rockenhaus.net/retractions/adrienne-rockenhaus/

faqs.question: Did Conrad Rockenhaus send Rob Hein a retraction demand?
faqs.answer: Yes. On June 30, 2026 he served a retraction demand, cease-funding notice, and litigation hold on Rob Hein as trustee under the same Michigan and Texas notice statutes. Executed PDFs: https://rockenhaus.net/retractions/rob-hein/

faqs.question: Where does Conrad Rockenhaus state he may file a federal defamation action?
faqs.answer: The June 30, 2026 retraction demands state an intended federal venue in the Western District of Texas, Waco Division, if statutory notice demands are not met. That is a stated intent in the demand letters, not a docketed federal case by itself. https://rockenhaus.net/retractions/

faqs.question: Did Conrad Rockenhaus serve statutory defamation notice before suing?
faqs.answer: He published and served formal June 30, 2026 retraction demands under MCL 600.2911(2)(b) and Texas Defamation Mitigation Act Sec. 73.055 (email and certified mail). Documents: https://rockenhaus.net/retractions/
